```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 6,
  dpi = 150,
  dev.args = list(bg = "linen")   # fill the margins left by fixed-shape maps
)

# In the PDF, scale every chart to the width of the text
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = "100%")
}

.old_plot_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {
  out <- .old_plot_hook(x, options)
  if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    out <- paste0('<div class="plot-frame">\n', out, '\n</div>')
  }
  out
})

library(here)
source(here("R", "load_packages.R"))
source(here("R", "config.R"))
source(here("R", "config_city.R"))
source(here("R", "theme.R"))
source(here("R", "get_data.R"))
source(here("R", "get_data_city.R"))
source(here("R", "process.R"))
source(here("R", "process_city.R"))

refresh <- isTRUE(params$refresh_data)
```

```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Downloads happen only on the first knit or when refresh_data is true.
city_geo     <- load_city_geo(refresh)
block_counts <- load_block_counts(refresh)

acs_bg_raw <- tryCatch(load_acs_bg(refresh), error = function(e) {
  warning(conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE); NULL })

ward_error <- NULL
districts <- tryCatch(load_districts(refresh), error = function(e) {
  ward_error <<- conditionMessage(e); NULL })

# ---- Block groups ----
bg_shapes  <- build_bg_shapes(city_geo)
bg_assign  <- assign_blocks(city_geo, bg_shapes, "bg", exact_2020_bg = TRUE)
bg_totals  <- summarise_totals(block_counts, bg_assign)
bg_compare <- compare_years(bg_totals) %>% mutate(label = bg_label(unit))
bg_age     <- summarise_age(block_counts, bg_assign) %>% mutate(label = bg_label(unit))

city_totals <- bg_totals %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(across(c(population, housing_units), sum), .groups = "drop")
city_pop <- function(y) city_totals$population[city_totals$year == y]
city_hu  <- function(y) city_totals$housing_units[city_totals$year == y]

bg_share <- bg_share_in_city(block_counts, city_geo)
bg_acs_ids <- bg_share$bg[bg_share$share_in_city >= bg_min_share_in_city]

bg_acs <- NULL
move_label <- NULL
if (!is.null(acs_bg_raw)) {
  bg_acs <- build_bg_acs(acs_bg_raw) %>%
    filter(geoid %in% bg_acs_ids) %>%
    mutate(label = bg_label(geoid))
  move_label <- recent_move_label(acs_bg_raw)
}

# Block groups ordered by 2020 population, largest first
bg_order <- bg_compare %>% arrange(desc(population_2020)) %>% pull(label)

# ---- Wards ----
ward_result <- if (!is.null(districts)) {
  build_wards(districts, city_geo$city)
} else {
  list(wards = NULL, message = paste("Ward boundaries could not be loaded:", ward_error))
}
wards <- ward_result$wards

if (!is.null(wards)) {
  ward_assign  <- assign_blocks(city_geo, wards, "ward")
  ward_compare <- summarise_totals(block_counts, ward_assign) %>%
    compare_years() %>%
    mutate(label = paste("Ward", unit))
  ward_age <- summarise_age(block_counts, ward_assign) %>%
    mutate(label = paste("Ward", unit))
  ward_coverage <- sum(ward_compare$population_2020) / city_pop(2020)
}
```

# About this report

This report looks inside the City of Kingston at two scales: Census block
groups, the smallest areas for which the American Community Survey publishes
data, and the city's wards. The 2020 Census counted
`r fmt_count(city_pop(2020))` residents in the city, compared with
`r fmt_count(city_pop(2010))` in 2010, and `r fmt_count(city_hu(2020))` housing
units, compared with `r fmt_count(city_hu(2010))`.

Both scales are built from census blocks, the smallest unit the Census Bureau
counts. Blocks are added up into today's (2020) block groups and today's ward
lines, so the 2010 and 2020 figures always describe the same territory even
where boundaries have been redrawn since 2010.

# Block groups

The city contains `r nrow(bg_shapes)` block groups, or parts of them. Labels
give the census tract and then the block-group number: **`r bg_order[1]`** is
block group `r sub(".*-", "", bg_order[1])` of tract `r sub("-.*", "", bg_order[1])`.

## Population change, 2010 to 2020

```{r bg-change-map, fig.height = 7.5}
bg_map_data <- bg_shapes %>% left_join(select(bg_compare, unit, pop_pct), by = c("bg" = "unit"))
lim <- max(abs(bg_map_data$pop_pct), na.rm = TRUE)

p <- ggplot(bg_map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pop_pct), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3)
if (!is.null(wards)) {
  p <- p + geom_sf(data = wards, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4, linetype = 2)
}
p +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.6, fun.geometry = sf::st_point_on_surface) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = c(-lim, lim),
                       name = "Population change (%)") +
  labs(title = "Population change by block group, 2010-2020",
       caption = paste0("Red = decline, blue = growth.",
                        if (!is.null(wards)) " Dashed lines are ward boundaries." else "",
                        "\nSource: 2010 and 2020 Census block counts, summed to 2020 block groups.")) +
  theme_kingston_map() +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```

```{r bg-change-table}
bg_compare %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = bg_order)) %>%
  arrange(label) %>%
  transmute(
    `Block group` = label,
    `2010` = fmt_count(population_2010),
    `2020` = fmt_count(population_2020),
    Change = fmt_count(pop_change),
    `Change (%)` = fmt_rate(pop_pct, 1),
    `Housing units 2010` = fmt_count(housing_units_2010),
    `Housing units 2020` = fmt_count(housing_units_2020),
    `Housing change (%)` = fmt_rate(hu_pct, 1)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrrrr",
               caption = "Residents and housing units by block group (parts inside the city)")
```

## Age, 2010 and 2020

```{r bg-age, fig.height = 7}
bg_age %>%
  filter(age_group %in% c("Under 18", "65 and over")) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rev(bg_order)),
         year = factor(year)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(share, label)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = label), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = year), size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ age_group) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("2010" = "grey55", "2020" = okabe_ito[["vermillion"]]),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Children and older residents by block group",
       x = "Share of residents", y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: 2010 and 2020 Census block counts (sex by age), summed to 2020 block groups.") +
  theme_kingston()
```

## Characteristics, `r period_label(bg_acs_year)`

```{r no-acs, eval = is.null(bg_acs), results = "asis"}
cat("*ACS block-group data could not be retrieved, so this section is empty.",
    "Check the Census API key and knit again with `refresh_data: true`.*")
```

```{r acs-intro, eval = !is.null(bg_acs), results = "asis"}
n_out <- nrow(bg_shapes) - length(unique(bg_acs$geoid))
cat("These figures come from the American Community Survey (ACS), ", period_label(bg_acs_year),
    ". Each block-group figure rests on a small sample of households pooled over five years, ",
    "so margins of error are wide; the chart after the maps shows them. ",
    "Grey areas on the maps have no estimate. ",
    "\"Moved in recently\" means the householder moved into the home in the most recent ",
    "category the Census Bureau reports (", tolower(move_label), ").",
    if (n_out > 0) paste0(" ", n_out, " block group(s) lying mostly outside the city are left out, ",
                          "because their ACS figures describe mostly non-city residents.") else "",
    sep = "")
```

```{r acs-maps, eval = !is.null(bg_acs), fig.height = 9}
map_indicators <- tibble::tribble(
  ~indicator,                               ~short,
  "Median household income",                "Median household income",
  "Renter-occupied (share of households)",  "Households renting",
  "Age: 65 and over",                       "Residents 65 and over",
  "Householder moved in recently",          "Householder moved in recently"
)

bg_fill_map <- function(indicator, short) {
  ind <- indicator
  d <- bg_shapes %>%
    left_join(filter(bg_acs, .data$indicator == ind) %>% select(geoid, estimate),
              by = c("bg" = "geoid"))
  is_money <- ind == "Median household income"
  ggplot(d) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = estimate), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.2, fun.geometry = sf::st_point_on_surface) +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlGnBu", direction = 1, na.value = "grey90",
                         labels = if (is_money) label_dollar(scale = 0.001, suffix = "k")
                                  else label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                         name = NULL) +
    labs(title = short) +
    theme_kingston_map(base_size = 9) +
    theme(legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.1)))
}

maps <- purrr::pmap(map_indicators, bg_fill_map)

# Four maps in a 2 x 2 grid without extra packages
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(2, 2)))
for (i in seq_along(maps)) {
  print(maps[[i]], vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = (i - 1) %/% 2 + 1,
                                       layout.pos.col = (i - 1) %% 2 + 1))
}
```

```{r acs-moe, eval = !is.null(bg_acs), fig.height = 8}
bg_acs %>%
  filter(indicator %in% map_indicators$indicator) %>%
  left_join(map_indicators, by = "indicator") %>%
  mutate(short = factor(short, levels = map_indicators$short),
         label = factor(label, levels = rev(bg_order)),
         reliability = if_else(!is.na(cv) & cv > 0.30, "Low (CV over 30%)", "Adequate")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(estimate)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(estimate, label)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = pmax(estimate - moe, 0), xmax = estimate + moe),
                 colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = reliability), size = 2.2, colour = okabe_ito[["blue"]], fill = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ short, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Adequate" = 19, "Low (CV over 30%)" = 21), name = "Reliability") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) {
    if (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 10) label_dollar()(x) else label_percent(accuracy = 1)(x)
  }) +
  labs(title = "The same figures with their margins of error",
       subtitle = "Lines show 90% intervals. Open circles: coefficient of variation above 30%; treat with caution.",
       x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Source: ACS 5-year estimates, ", period_label(bg_acs_year),
                        ", tables B01001, B19013, B25003 and B25038.")) +
  theme_kingston()
```

# Wards

```{r ward-message, results = "asis"}
cat("*", ward_result$message, "*", sep = "")
if (!is.null(wards) && abs(ward_coverage - 1) > 0.01) {
  cat(" *The wards account for ", fmt_share(ward_coverage),
      " of the city's 2020 population; the rest falls in blocks the ward map ",
      "does not cover.*", sep = "")
}
```

```{r ward-intro, eval = !is.null(wards), results = "asis"}
cat("Ward lines are redrawn after each census, so these are today's wards. ",
    "The 2010 figures are the people who lived, in 2010, inside today's ward lines.",
    sep = "")
```

```{r ward-map, eval = !is.null(wards), fig.height = 7.5}
ward_map_data <- wards %>%
  left_join(select(ward_compare, unit, population_2020, pop_pct), by = c("ward" = "unit")) %>%
  mutate(map_label = paste0(label, "\n", fmt_count(population_2020), "\n", fmt_rate(pop_pct, 1)))
wlim <- max(abs(ward_map_data$pop_pct), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(ward_map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pop_pct), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = map_label), size = 3, fun.geometry = sf::st_point_on_surface,
               lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = c(-wlim, wlim),
                       name = "Population change 2010-2020 (%)") +
  labs(title = "Wards: 2020 population and change since 2010",
       caption = "Source: 2010 and 2020 Census block counts, summed to current ward boundaries.") +
  theme_kingston_map() +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"))
```

```{r ward-table, eval = !is.null(wards)}
ward_compare %>%
  arrange(unit) %>%
  transmute(
    Ward = label,
    `2010` = fmt_count(population_2010),
    `2020` = fmt_count(population_2020),
    `Change (%)` = fmt_rate(pop_pct, 1),
    `Share of city 2020` = fmt_share(share_of_city),
    `Housing units 2010` = fmt_count(housing_units_2010),
    `Housing units 2020` = fmt_count(housing_units_2020),
    `Housing change (%)` = fmt_rate(hu_pct, 1)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrrrr", caption = "Residents and housing units by ward")
```

```{r ward-age, eval = !is.null(wards), fig.height = 5}
ward_levels <- paste("Ward", sort(unique(ward_age$unit), decreasing = TRUE))

ward_age %>%
  filter(age_group %in% c("Under 18", "65 and over")) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = ward_levels), year = factor(year)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(share, label)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = label), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = year), size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ age_group) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("2010" = "grey55", "2020" = okabe_ito[["vermillion"]]),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Children and older residents by ward",
       x = "Share of residents", y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: 2010 and 2020 Census block counts (sex by age), summed to current wards.") +
  theme_kingston()
```

# Notes on the data

- **Census blocks** are the building blocks for both scales. Each 2020 block
  belongs to exactly one 2020 block group. Each 2010 block is placed by a point
  inside it. That is exact unless a 2010 block was later split by a new
  boundary, which in a built-up city is uncommon.
- **2020 counts** include noise added for privacy (differential privacy). It
  is noticeable for a single block and shrinks as blocks are added together;
  at the size of a block group or ward it is small. Housing-unit totals were
  not altered.
- **ACS figures** are survey estimates, shown with 90% margins of error. The
  coefficient of variation (standard error divided by the estimate) above 30%
  is a common threshold for "use with caution". Medians that the Census Bureau
  suppressed appear blank on the maps.
- **Ward boundaries** come from the Ulster County Board of Elections'
  election-district file, merged into wards
  (`r if (is.null(ward_file)) "downloaded automatically" else "from your own file"`).
- **Data versions:** 2010 and 2020 Census; ACS 5-year `r period_label(bg_acs_year)`;
  2020 TIGER/Line boundaries.

# Sources

U.S. Census Bureau: 2010 Census Summary File 1 and 2020 Census Demographic and
Housing Characteristics File (block level); American Community Survey 5-year
estimates; 2010 and 2020 TIGER/Line block and county subdivision boundaries.
Ulster County Information Services: election district boundaries. Data
retrieved with the tidycensus and tigris R packages.
